additionalProperties.description: Keyed by its id: a slug (shop-api; letters, digits, - . _) given once. Never change or reuse it; rename with name.

kind.description: actor: a person or role. system: a product or service as a whole. app: something that runs (a service, job, web app). store: where data rests (database, bucket, topic). component: a part inside an app. module: a package, crate, folder or source file (has a path). function: anything callable in the code (function, method, handler, job, script), inside its file module. library: a third-party package the code uses (has a package). table: a table, collection or dataset table, inside its store, with its columns listed on it (one box per table); a foreign key or a pointer to a row elsewhere is a connection to the other table that names its column.

name.description: What people call it. Leave out when it's the same as the id.

in.description: The id of the object this one lives inside (apps and stores in a system, components in an app). Leave out for top level.

context.description: Everything about it, in markdown: what it does and why first (a sentence or two), then whatever helps (examples, payloads and data shapes, decisions, open questions, how to build it). Not drawn; show gives it in full.

tech.description: Languages, frameworks or products: [Go, Cloud Run].

icon.description: The logo to show when the one guessed from tech is wrong: a technology ("rust"), or "none" for no logo.

path.description: A module's place in its repo: repo:path (s-chan:crates/board/src/main.rs). It decides the module's file: code/<repo>/<path>.yaml for a source file, code/<repo>/<path>/_.yaml for a folder or package; its functions and their calls live there too.

signature.description: A function's inputs and what it returns: "(Cart, UserId) -> Order" (a name on an input is optional: "(cart: Cart)"). Quote it. The entities it names are its entities: don't list them in uses.

uses.description: Entities it works with that its signature doesn't name, by name: [Order, Ledger]. A name nothing defines yet becomes a TBD entity.

package.description: A library's package. Libraries live in libraries.yaml.

type.description: Its type as the database says it (uuid, text, timestamptz, vector(512)).

personal.description: Holds data about a person: a key from it across regions is a residency warning.

description.description: A sentence about it, when the name doesn't say.

columns.description: A table's columns, in order. Shown in its panel and given to agents; never drawn as boxes. A foreign key is a connection to the other table with column (and to_column).

status.description: Leave out for live. future: decided, not built. deprecated: still there, being retired. removed: gone (kept for history; drawn only where a rule asks for status: removed). Never delete an object for being gone.

external.description: Run by someone else (a vendor, a customer).

tags.description: Lowercase labels. group:value for a tag group declared in archnm.yaml (personal-data:holds, owner:signals); the value must be one the group lists.

refs.description: Identifiers in other systems (sys: SYS-5, key: P4). Fields archnm.yaml protects are changed only by people.

sources.description: Where the facts come from, so a person or a drift job can check them: repo@ref:path[:line[-line]] (ref: a sha or a branch, on GitHub under archnm.yaml's github), repo:path for a file that isn't written yet, or an http(s) address.

items.description: Exactly one of link, image, doc, code, dependency, and an optional title.

link.description: An http or https address (a runbook, an RFC, a dashboard).

image.description: A picture of it: an http(s) address, or a file in the design (assets/erd.png).

doc.description: A markdown file in the design (docs/auth.md).

code.description: Where it is in the code: repo:path, repo:path#L12 or repo:path#function.

dependency.description: A library it uses: the library object's id. Every node using that library is found from it.

title.description: What to call it; defaults to the address or path.

references.description: What it points at outside the model, shown in its panel: links, images, docs, code, dependencies. One per target.

notes.description: Its running doc, in markdown: what's still needed, open questions, a checklist (- [ ] …). Not drawn. Comments pinned on a diagram are separate.

guess.description: true when it's believed but not confirmed (an agent inferred it); drawn fainter. Leave out once confirmed.

objects.description: The objects in this file, by id: a top-level object and everything inside it, or (_top.yaml) the top-level objects with nothing inside.

additionalProperties.description: Keyed by its name as code writes it (PaidOrder): that name is its id, and what everything else uses to point at it.

in.description: The id of the box that defines it (Order in the orders service). Leave out when nothing owns it yet.

extends.description: Entities it inherits from, or (an interface) implements, by name: [Order].

context.description: What it is and anything worth knowing, in markdown.

fields.description: Name → type: { id: uuid, items: "[OrderItem]", note: text? }. A key with ( ) is a method ("charge(amount: Money)": Receipt), which makes it an interface. A type that's another entity's name links to it.

values.description: An enum's values (pending, paid, cancelled), instead of fields.

entities.description: The entities the boxes in this file define (DTOs, interfaces, enums), by name. With no fields or values, it's TBD: a name to fill in later.

from.description: The caller's id. A connection lives in the caller's file.

label.description: What it does, as a short verb phrase ("reads orders").

context.description: For agents, in markdown: what travels over it (example requests and responses, payload shapes, auth, errors, retries). Not drawn; show gives it in full.

status.description: Leave out for live; as for objects.

via.description: An object the traffic passes through on the way (a load balancer, a gateway). Draw the connection to the real backend and name the middle here.

sources.description: Where the facts come from, so a person or a drift job can check them: repo@ref:path[:line[-line]] (ref: a sha or a branch, on GitHub under archnm.yaml's github), repo:path for a file that isn't written yet, or an http(s) address.

guess.description: true when it's believed but not confirmed (an importer matched the call by name, an agent inferred it); drawn fainter. Leave out once confirmed.

column.description: Between tables, a foreign key or pointer: the column on the from table that holds it (customer_id). The line is labelled with it.

to_column.description: The column on the to table it points at; leave out for its primary key.

carries.description: The entities that travel over it, by name: [PaidOrder]. A name nothing defines yet becomes a TBD entity.

items.description: Exactly one of link, image, doc, code, dependency, and an optional title.

link.description: An http or https address (a runbook, an RFC, a dashboard).

image.description: A picture of it: an http(s) address, or a file in the design (assets/erd.png).

doc.description: A markdown file in the design (docs/auth.md).

code.description: Where it is in the code: repo:path, repo:path#L12 or repo:path#function.

dependency.description: A library it uses: the library object's id. Every node using that library is found from it.

title.description: What to call it; defaults to the address or path.

references.description: What it points at: links, docs, code, images. One per target.

notes.description: Its running doc, in markdown, as an object's: what's still needed, open questions, a checklist. Not drawn. Comments pinned to its arrow are separate.

connections.description: Connections whose caller is in this file, one line each.
